            manifest.update(completed_steps=step, tokens_processed=exposures, updated_at=now(),
                            elapsed_seconds=elapsed_before+time.perf_counter()-started,phase="Training the decoder",

            write_json(directory / "manifest.json", manifest)

        model.load_state_dict(state["model"])

        baselines = {s: baseline.evaluate(rows, tokenizer, s) for s in ("dev", "test")}
        write_json(directory / "evaluation.json", {"checkpoint_step": state["step"], "transformer": evaluations,
                   "bigram": baselines, "selection": "lowest dev NLL; never selected on test",
                   "units": "nats per shared BPE next-token target; lower is better"})

        torch.manual_seed(seed + 100)
        prompts = ["The model", "A source", "Training"]

                   "temperature": 0.8, "top_k": 20, "max_new_tokens": 80, "seed": seed + 100,
                   "note": "Sequential samples share one seeded RNG stream; not independent reseeding."} for p in prompts])

                        error=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", updated_at=now(),

optimizer.label: Optimizer
optimizer.explanation: The rule that converts gradients into weight changes. AdamW tracks moving statistics; plain SGD does not.
optimizer.equation: SGD: w_next = w - ηg. AdamW: rescaled moving-gradient update plus decoupled weight decay.
effects: The same learning rate need not suit both optimizers.
AdamW uses additional state for each parameter.
interactions: A one-rate comparison tests these configurations, not the universally best optimizer.
Weight decay in SGD is coupled L2 here; AdamW decay is decoupled.

weight_decay.label: Weight decay / L2 coefficient
weight_decay.explanation: A pressure toward smaller weights. Here it applies to every parameter, including normalization and embeddings.
weight_decay.equation: AdamW decay contribution: w_next ≈ (1 - ηλ)w + gradient update; λ = decay coefficient.
effects: May reduce overfitting; too much can suppress useful learning.
This is not the same mechanism as randomly dropping activations.
interactions: Its effect depends on learning rate and number of updates.
The implementation differs between AdamW and SGD.

clip_norm.label: Gradient clipping limit
clip_norm.explanation: Limit the total gradient norm before the optimizer step. Zero explicitly disables clipping.
clip_norm.equation: g_clipped = g × min(1, c / ||g||); c = clipping threshold.
effects: Can limit a large gradient spike.
A small threshold can restrict useful updates; clipping is not a guarantee against divergence.
interactions: Inspect the recorded pre-clip norm.
A high learning rate can still cause trouble after gradients are clipped.

def clip_gradients(model, limit):

schedule.label: Learning-rate schedule
schedule.explanation: How the learning rate changes after optional warmup. The horizon is fixed separately so restart does not silently change it.
schedule.equation: cosine multiplier = 0.1 + 0.9 × (1 + cos(πp))/2; p = progress after warmup, capped at 1.
effects: Decay makes later updates smaller, which may stabilize fitting.
It can also slow learning too early.
interactions: Schedule horizon is measured in optimizer updates, not tokens.
Changing batch/context changes how much data is seen before decay.

warmup_steps.label: Warmup updates
warmup_steps.explanation: Start at a fraction of the peak learning rate, then increase linearly.
warmup_steps.equation: During warmup: η(step) = peak_rate × step / warmup_updates.
effects: Can soften early updates.
Too much warmup in a short run can spend most of the run learning slowly.
interactions: Warmup must be shorter than the schedule horizon.
Warmup also applies before a constant post-warmup schedule.

schedule_steps.label: Schedule horizon
schedule_steps.explanation: The update at which cosine decay reaches its minimum. It is independent of when a run is interrupted.
effects: A longer horizon decays more slowly.
With a constant schedule and no warmup it does not affect updates.
interactions: Keep the horizon fixed when checking resume equality.
Interpret this together with total updates and token exposure.

dropout.label: Dropout
dropout.explanation: Randomly zero some attention/MLP activations during training. It is disabled for evaluation and generation.
dropout.equation: training output = mask × activation / (1-p); p = dropout probability.
effects: Can discourage reliance on particular activations.
Too much can make fitting difficult; it does not add data.
interactions: Larger models/smaller datasets may overfit more.
Training loss with dropout is not directly the same estimator as full evaluation-mode loss.

block_size.label: Context window (tokens)
block_size.explanation: The maximum number of input tokens in one training window. Longer documents are chunked without crossing document boundaries.
block_size.equation: attention score elements = batch × heads × T²; T = context length.
effects: Longer context can expose more preceding information.
It increases attention cost and changes window/chunk boundaries.
interactions: A tokenizer change alters how much text fits into T tokens.
At fixed updates, context also changes token exposure and position-embedding count.

        future = torch.ones(t, t, device=x.device, dtype=torch.bool).triu(1)
        weights = scores.masked_fill(future, float("-inf")).softmax(dim=-1)

width.label: Hidden width
width.explanation: How many numbers describe a token inside the model.
width.equation: A dense decoder block has roughly 12d² matrix weights; d = hidden width.
effects: More width increases capacity and compute, not guaranteed held-out quality.
A tiny corpus may let a wider model memorize faster.
interactions: Width must be divisible by attention heads.
Width and number of layers jointly change parameter count and optimization.

layers.label: Decoder layers
layers.explanation: How many attention-plus-MLP blocks process the representation in sequence.
layers.equation: x_(layer+1) = block_layer(x_layer); deeper models repeat this computation.
effects: Adds representational capacity and training work.
More depth can make optimization harder.
interactions: Residual paths and normalization help signals travel through depth.
This is not a parameter-matched depth comparison unless width is adjusted.

residuals.explanation: Add each block's input back to its transformed output. Turning them off creates an educational ablation.

normalization.label: Normalization
normalization.explanation: Rescale a token's hidden features before each sublayer. LayerNorm also subtracts the feature mean; RMSNorm does not.
normalization.equation: RMSNorm(x) = gain × x / √(mean(x²)+ε); LayerNorm centers x before scaling.
effects: May help keep optimization well behaved.

interactions: Learning rate, residuals and depth interact with stability.

merges.label: BPE merge operations
merges.explanation: How many frequent byte pairs the tokenizer may merge, fitted on training documents only. Zero means UTF-8 byte tokens.
merges.equation: vocabulary = 259 + completed_merges (three special IDs plus 256 bytes).
effects: More merges often shorten token sequences but expand the vocabulary.
Changing the tokenizer changes the unit of per-token loss.

train_fraction.label: Training document fraction
train_fraction.explanation: Use a deterministic prefix of the authored training documents. Dev/test text remains fixed. This is not a random representative sample.
effects: Less data may encourage memorization and reduce topic coverage.
More updates on fewer documents repeat information rather than add it.
interactions: The tokenizer is refitted on the selected train documents.

seed.label: Random seed

seed.equation: same code + config + data + restored state → tested CPU repeatability; not universal hardware determinism.

Repeated runs help reveal variation but three seeds are still limited evidence.
interactions: Changing architecture consumes random numbers differently.

def train(name, preset="tiny", steps=None, seed=17, device="auto", resume=False,
          corpus=None, runs_root=RUNS, overrides=None, learning=None):
    if preset not in PRESETS:
        raise ValueError("Choose smoke or tiny.")
    settings = {**DEFAULTS, **PRESETS[preset]}
    settings["seed"], settings["device"] = seed, device
    if overrides is not None:
        settings = validate(overrides)
        seed, device = settings["seed"], settings["device"]
    steps = settings["steps"] if steps is None else steps
    if not isinstance(steps, int) or not 1 <= steps <= 2000:
        raise ValueError("This local lab allows 1–2000 optimizer steps per run.")
    if not isinstance(seed, int) or not 0 <= seed <= 2**31 - 1:
        raise ValueError("Seed must be an integer in [0, 2^31-1].")
    corpus = Path(corpus or ROOT / "data" / "corpus.jsonl")
    rows = load_corpus(corpus)
    rows = select_training_data(rows, settings["train_fraction"])
    device = choose_device(device)
    torch.set_num_threads(1)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    random.seed(seed)
    tokenizer = ByteBPE.fit([r["text"] for r in rows if r["split"] == "train"], settings["merges"])
    config = {"preset": preset, "seed": seed, "learning_rate": settings["learning_rate"],
              "batch_size": settings["batch_size"], "accumulation": settings["accumulation"],
              "optimizer":settings["optimizer"], "weight_decay":settings["weight_decay"],
              "clip_norm":settings["clip_norm"], "schedule":settings["schedule"],
              "warmup_steps":settings["warmup_steps"], "schedule_steps":settings["schedule_steps"],
              "train_fraction":settings["train_fraction"],
              "corpus_sha256": sha256(corpus), "tokenizer": tokenizer.to_dict(),
              "model": asdict(ModelConfig(tokenizer.vocab_size, settings["block_size"], settings["width"],
                                          settings["layers"], settings["heads"], settings["dropout"],
                                          settings["positions"],settings["residuals"],settings["normalization"]))}
    directory = run_path(name, runs_root)
    if resume:
        verify(directory)
        previous = read_json(directory / "manifest.json")
        if previous["config"] != config or previous["hardware"]["device"] != device:
            raise ValueError("Resume requires identical config, data, seed and device.")
        if previous["source_hashes"] != source_hashes():
            raise ValueError("Source changed since checkpoint; start a new run instead of silently resuming.")
    else:
        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    model = TinyDecoder(ModelConfig(**config["model"])).to(device)
    optimizer = make_optimizer(model, config)
    sampler = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed + 1)
    start_step, exposures, best_dev, metrics = 0, 0, float("inf"), []
    if resume:
        state = torch.load(directory / "last.pt", map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
        model.load_state_dict(state["model"])
        optimizer.load_state_dict(state["optimizer"])
        sampler.set_state(state["sampler_rng"])
        torch.set_rng_state(state["torch_rng"])
        if device == "mps":
            torch.mps.set_rng_state(state["mps_rng"])
        if device == "cuda":
            torch.cuda.set_rng_state(state["cuda_rng"])
        start_step, exposures, best_dev = state["step"], state["tokens_processed"], state["best_dev"]
        if steps <= start_step:
            raise ValueError("Resume steps is the TOTAL target, and must exceed the saved step.")
        metrics = read_json(directory / "metrics.json")
    split_items = {s: examples(rows, tokenizer, s, settings["block_size"]) for s in ("train", "dev", "test")}
    baseline = Bigram(tokenizer.vocab_size).fit(rows, tokenizer)
    manifest = {"schema_version": 2, "id": name, "status": "RUNNING", "purpose": "educational_pretraining",
                "started_at": previous["started_at"] if resume else now(), "updated_at": now(),
                "resumed": resume, "requested_steps": steps, "completed_steps": start_step,
                "config": config, "model": model.description(), "source_hashes": source_hashes(),
                "settings":{**settings,"steps":steps,"seed":seed,"device":device}, "learning":learning or {},
                "evaluation_protocol":"document_chunks_v1", "metric_definition":"next-token NLL including EOS; excludes PAD/BOS",
                "hardware": {"device": device, "machine": platform.machine(), "python": platform.python_version(),
                             "torch": str(torch.__version__), "threads": 1},
                "limits": ["Authored miniature corpus, not general language competence.",
                           "Development loss selects checkpoint; test is evaluated only at run completion.",
                           "Same-tokenizer bigram baseline; training compute and model capacity differ.",
                           "Fixed synthetic splits share templates; exact dedup is not semantic dedup.",
                           "CPU restart equivalence tested; accelerator bitwise determinism not promised."]}
    write_json(directory / "manifest.json", manifest)
    write_json(directory / "tokenizer.json", tokenizer.to_dict())
    write_json(directory / "data.json", {"license": "CC0-1.0 authored synthetic learning fixture",
                                        "documents": rows, "counts": dict(Counter(r["split"] for r in rows)),
                                        "duplicates": 0, "audit": "NFKC + casefold + whitespace exact dedup only"})
    write_json(directory / "metrics.json", metrics)
    elapsed_before = previous.get("training_seconds", 0) if resume else 0
    started = time.perf_counter()
    telemetry=Telemetry(directory)
    try:
        for step in range(start_step + 1, steps + 1):
            model.train()
            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            current_lr = learning_rate_at(step, config)
            for group in optimizer.param_groups:
                group["lr"] = current_lr
            microbatches = []
            for _ in range(config["accumulation"]):
                indices = torch.randint(len(split_items["train"]), (config["batch_size"],), generator=sampler)
                microbatches.append(batch([split_items["train"][i] for i in indices.tolist()], device))
            # Divide by ALL valid tokens, not an average of unequal microbatch means.
            valid_total = sum(int((y != -100).sum()) for _, y in microbatches)
            summed_loss = 0.0
            for x, y in microbatches:
                loss, count = loss_sum(model(x), y)
                if not torch.isfinite(loss):
                    raise FloatingPointError("Non-finite loss; run stopped.")
                (loss / valid_total).backward()
                summed_loss += loss.item()
            grad_norm = clip_gradients(model, config["clip_norm"])
            if not math.isfinite(grad_norm):
                raise FloatingPointError("Non-finite gradients; run stopped.")
            optimizer.step()
            exposures += valid_total
            row={"step":step,"sampled_train_nll":summed_loss/valid_total,
                 "gradient_norm_pre_clip":grad_norm,"learning_rate":current_lr,"tokens_processed":exposures,
                 "elapsed_seconds":elapsed_before+time.perf_counter()-started,
                 "tokens_per_second":(exposures-state["tokens_processed"] if resume else exposures)/max(time.perf_counter()-started,1e-6)}
            if step == 1 or step % 20 == 0 or step == steps:
                dev = evaluate(model, split_items["dev"], device)
                train_eval = evaluate(model, split_items["train"], device)
                row.update(train_nll=train_eval["nll"],dev_nll=dev["nll"])
                if dev["nll"] < best_dev:
                    best_dev = dev["nll"]
                    save_checkpoint(directory / "best.pt", model, optimizer, sampler, step, exposures, best_dev, config)
            metrics.append(row);telemetry.log(row)
            # A resumable last checkpoint is recorded for EVERY completed optimizer step.
            save_checkpoint(directory / "last.pt", model, optimizer, sampler, step, exposures, best_dev, config)
            manifest.update(completed_steps=step, tokens_processed=exposures, updated_at=now(),
                            elapsed_seconds=elapsed_before+time.perf_counter()-started,phase="Training the decoder",
                            tokens_per_second=row["tokens_per_second"],
                            eta_seconds=(time.perf_counter()-started)/(step-start_step)*(steps-step))
            write_json(directory / "metrics.json", metrics)
            write_json(directory / "manifest.json", manifest)
        synchronize(device)
        manifest["training_seconds"] = elapsed_before + time.perf_counter() - started
        state = torch.load(directory / "best.pt", map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
        model.load_state_dict(state["model"])
        evaluations = {s: evaluate(model, split_items[s], device) for s in ("train", "dev", "test")}
        for split, result in evaluations.items():
            byte_count = sum(len(r["text"].encode("utf-8")) for r in rows if r["split"] == split)
            result["utf8_bytes"] = byte_count
            result["bits_per_byte"] = result["nll"] * result["tokens"] / (byte_count * math.log(2))
        baselines = {s: baseline.evaluate(rows, tokenizer, s) for s in ("dev", "test")}
        write_json(directory / "evaluation.json", {"checkpoint_step": state["step"], "transformer": evaluations,
                   "bigram": baselines, "selection": "lowest dev NLL; never selected on test",
                   "units": "nats per shared BPE next-token target; lower is better"})
        write_json(directory / "inspection.json", inspect_model(model, tokenizer))
        torch.manual_seed(seed + 100)
        prompts = ["The model", "A source", "Training"]
        write_json(directory / "samples.json", [{"prompt": p, "completion": generate(model, tokenizer, p),
                   "temperature": 0.8, "top_k": 20, "max_new_tokens": 80, "seed": seed + 100,
                   "note": "Sequential samples share one seeded RNG stream; not independent reseeding."} for p in prompts])
        manifest.update(status="MEASURED", best_checkpoint_step=state["step"], finished_at=now(), updated_at=now())
    except BaseException as exc:
        synchronize(device)
        manifest.update(status="CANCELLED" if isinstance(exc, KeyboardInterrupt) else "FAILED",
                        error=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", updated_at=now(),
                        training_seconds=elapsed_before + time.perf_counter() - started)
        raise
    finally:
        telemetry.close()
        write_json(directory / "manifest.json", manifest)
        seal(directory)
    return manifest

methods.name: Constant baseline
methods.meaning: Most frequent training class, or mean training rating. Checks whether learned features add value.

methods.name: Logistic regression
methods.meaning: A linear score per class becomes normalized class probabilities. Minimize regularized log loss.

methods.name: Ridge regression
methods.meaning: A weighted feature sum fitted with squared error and an L2 penalty. λ=0 removes the penalty.

methods.name: Lasso regression
methods.meaning: Squared error plus an L1 penalty that can set coefficients to zero.

methods.name: Elastic net
methods.meaning: Combine L1 sparsity and L2 shrinkage in a linear predictor.

methods.name: Nearest neighbours
methods.meaning: Store training rows; classify a new row using nearby examples in the chosen feature space.

methods.name: Support vector machine
methods.meaning: Fit a margin-based decision rule or epsilon-insensitive regression; an RBF kernel allows nonlinear patterns.

methods.name: Gaussian Naive Bayes
methods.meaning: Combine class-conditional Gaussian feature likelihoods under a conditional-independence assumption.

methods.name: Decision tree
methods.meaning: Repeatedly split feature values to create locally constant prediction regions.

methods.name: Random forest
methods.meaning: Average many randomized, bootstrapped trees to reduce individual-tree variance.

methods.name: Histogram gradient boosting
methods.meaning: Add trees sequentially to reduce the current loss. A fixed round budget is used here.

methods.name: K-means
methods.meaning: Assign each row to a nearby fitted center, minimizing within-group squared distance. Labels never enter fitting.

methods.name: Gaussian mixture
methods.meaning: Fit a probabilistic mixture of Gaussian components by expectation maximization.

methods.name: DBSCAN
methods.meaning: Connect dense neighbourhoods and mark sparse points as noise. No native held-out prediction; fitting-set diagnostics only.

methods.name: Principal component analysis
methods.meaning: Fit high-variance directions on training rows, project and reconstruct separate rows. No target labels are used.

methods.name: Isolation Forest
methods.meaning: Random partitions isolate unusual examples in fewer splits. Generated noise labels are available only for diagnostics.

methods.name: Linear neural baseline
methods.meaning: One learned linear layer; a useful same-training-loop baseline, not a deep architecture.

methods.name: Multilayer perceptron
methods.meaning: Alternate learned dense layers and nonlinear activations. Flatten images; standardize numeric features using training rows.

methods.name: Convolutional network
methods.meaning: Two spatial convolution blocks share filters across image positions, pool locally, then classify the retained feature map.

methods.name: Residual convolutional network
methods.meaning: Add an identity shortcut around two same-shape convolutions so each block can learn a correction.

methods.name: Dense autoencoder
methods.meaning: Compress images into a learned bottleneck and reconstruct the original pixel values. Targets are input pixels, not class labels.

width.label: Encoder hidden width
width.definition: Dense hidden width before and after the smaller bottleneck.
width.effect: The bottleneck has max(2, width / 4) units, rounded down. Larger widths increase capacity and reconstruction cost.

methods.name: Residual MLP
methods.meaning: Project inputs to a hidden vector, then refine it with additive two-layer residual blocks. A tabular/image comparison with a plain MLP; not parameter matched.

layers.label: Residual blocks
layers.definition: Each block contains two dense transformations and an additive shortcut.
layers.effect: More blocks add depth and parameters; this count is not the number of individual linear layers.

methods.name: LeNet-style CNN
methods.meaning: Two 5×5 convolution/pooling stages and a small dense head. Adapted to 8×8, 28×28 or 32×32 inputs; not an exact reproduction of historical LeNet-5.

methods.name: Convolutional autoencoder
methods.meaning: Downsample pixels into a smaller spatial representation, then reconstruct with transposed convolutions. No class labels enter the loss.

width.label: Encoder channels
width.definition: Channels in the first stride-2 convolution; the next layer has max(2, width / 16) channels, rounded down.
width.effect: The encoder halves the spatial size twice; transposed convolutions reconstruct the pixels. This is not the classifier CNN's doubled-channel second block.

methods.name: RNN
methods.meaning: Apply a tanh update to the current input and previous hidden state, without LSTM/GRU gates. Use the final recurrent state for prediction. Text padding is excluded with packed sequences; images are read one horizontal row at a time.

width.label: Recurrent hidden width
width.definition: Hidden coordinates per direction; bidirectional models concatenate two such vectors.
width.effect: Doubling directions increases parameters and head input size.

layers.label: Stacked recurrent layers
layers.definition: Pass the sequence of hidden states into the next recurrent layer.
layers.effect: Dropout applies between layers when depth exceeds one, and before the prediction head at every depth.

methods.name: Bidirectional RNN
methods.meaning: Apply a tanh update to the current input and previous hidden state, without LSTM/GRU gates. Read the supplied history in both directions, then concatenate the final forward/backward states. This never exposes future target hours. layers.label: Stacked recurrent layers
layers.definition: Pass the sequence of hidden states into the next recurrent layer.
layers.effect: Dropout applies between layers when depth exceeds one, and before the prediction head at every depth.

methods.name: 1D convolutional encoder
methods.meaning: Learn local patterns along token positions or sensor/time steps. Mask text padding after each layer; pool valid positions for classification, read the last position for forecasting.

width.label: Hidden channels / coordinates
width.definition: Working width of sequence features or patch vectors.
width.effect: Larger width increases capacity and computation.

layers.label: Convolution layers
layers.definition: Repeated encoder transformations; TCN blocks contain two causal convolutions each.
layers.effect: More blocks increase depth; no pretrained layers are used.

methods.name: Temporal convolutional network
methods.meaning: Stack residual blocks with two causal convolutions each. Dilation doubles across blocks, expanding past context without recurrent updates. Forecasting reads the final history state.

width.label: Hidden channels / coordinates
width.definition: Working width of sequence features or patch vectors.
width.effect: Larger width increases capacity and computation.

layers.label: Encoder blocks
layers.definition: Repeated encoder transformations; TCN blocks contain two causal convolutions each.
layers.effect: More blocks increase depth; no pretrained layers are used.

methods.name: Small Transformer encoder
methods.meaning: Use bidirectional self-attention over the supplied input only, followed by position-wise MLPs and residual paths. Mask padded text. This is trained from scratch, not a pretrained language model.

width.label: Hidden channels / coordinates
width.definition: Working width of sequence features or patch vectors.
width.effect: Larger width increases capacity and computation.

layers.label: Encoder blocks
layers.definition: Repeated encoder transformations; TCN blocks contain two causal convolutions each.
layers.effect: More blocks increase depth; no pretrained layers are used.

methods.name: Mean token embeddings
methods.meaning: Average learned embeddings over real tokens, ignoring padding and word order, then classify. A simple baseline for sequence models on SMS.

methods.name: Tiny Vision Transformer
methods.meaning: Project non-overlapping image patches to vectors, add positions, apply self-attention blocks, mean-pool and classify. Small and trained from scratch; no pretrained ViT weights or foundation-model performance claims.

width.label: Hidden channels / coordinates
width.definition: Working width of sequence features or patch vectors.
width.effect: Larger width increases capacity and computation.

layers.label: Encoder blocks
layers.definition: Repeated encoder transformations; TCN blocks contain two causal convolutions each.
layers.effect: More blocks increase depth; no pretrained layers are used.

methods.name: TF-IDF + logistic regression
methods.meaning: Fit a sparse token/word-pair vocabulary and inverse-document frequencies on training texts, then learn a linear classifier. A strong low-cost text baseline.

methods.name: TF-IDF + Multinomial Naive Bayes
methods.meaning: Fit training-only nonnegative TF-IDF features and a smoothed class-conditional word model. Compare with neural models before assuming sequence complexity helps.

max_tokens.label: Maximum tokens per message
max_tokens.definition: Keep this many leading word/punctuation tokens; shorter messages get masked right padding.
max_tokens.effect: A longer limit keeps more text but increases computation. This is not a pretrained model's subword tokenizer.

vocab_size.label: Maximum vocabulary entries
vocab_size.definition: Keep the most frequent training tokens. Neural vocabularies reserve PAD=0 and UNK=1; TF-IDF uses this as its feature cap.
vocab_size.effect: Rare or unseen words lose detail. Development/test texts never choose the vocabulary.

embedding_dim.label: Token embedding width
embedding_dim.definition: Number of learned coordinates representing each token.
embedding_dim.effect: Embeddings start randomly and learn during this experiment; larger width increases parameters.

lookback.label: Past hours used
lookback.definition: Predict the next hour using this many consecutive observed hourly counts.
lookback.effect: Longer history can capture daily patterns. All lookbacks use the same eligible target hours and chronological splits.

kernel_size.label: 1D filter width
kernel_size.definition: Number of neighbouring sequence positions read by each convolution.
kernel_size.effect: Wider filters see more nearby steps. TCN uses causal filters with dilation doubling across blocks.

heads.label: Attention heads
heads.definition: Split the hidden coordinates into parallel attention heads; hidden width must divide evenly.
heads.effect: More heads change how features are grouped, not the total hidden width or automatically the quality.

positions.label: Learn position embeddings
positions.definition: Add a trainable vector for each sequence or patch position before attention.
positions.effect: Without positions, mean-pooled attention cannot distinguish permutations of otherwise identical tokens/patches.

patch_size.label: ViT patch side in pixels
patch_size.definition: A square patch is projected to one vector. Patch side must divide both image dimensions.
patch_size.effect: Smaller patches retain finer layout but create more tokens and quadratic attention cost.
patch_size.equation: patch tokens = (image height / patch side) × (image width / patch side)

ngrams.label: TF-IDF word features
ngrams.definition: One uses individual tokens; two adds adjacent two-token combinations.
ngrams.effect: Bigrams add local order but consume the same feature budget.

alpha.label: Naive Bayes smoothing α
alpha.definition: Adds pseudo-counts when estimating class-conditional word weights.
alpha.effect: Avoids zero-probability features; excessive smoothing can erase distinctions.

train_limit.label: Maximum training rows
train_limit.definition: Cap only fitting examples; development and test remain fixed.
train_limit.effect: More examples cost more computation. Different caps are data-budget comparisons, not isolated model changes.

seed.label: Model seed
seed.definition: Initializes model weights, fitting randomness and minibatch order, not the split.
seed.effect: Repeat seeds to measure variation. The split seed stays fixed at 20261102.

scaling.label: Feature scaling
scaling.definition: Fit a feature transform using training rows only, then apply it unchanged to development/test.
scaling.effect: Scaling changes distances and the effective strength of regularization; trees usually do not need it.
scaling.equation: standard: z = (x − training mean) / training standard deviation

strength.label: Regularization strength λ
strength.definition: A penalty discouraging large coefficients; the exact objective differs for ridge, lasso and elastic net.
strength.effect: Larger penalties can reduce variance but also erase useful signal. This λ is not the SVM/logistic C.

C.label: Inverse regularization C
C.definition: scikit-learn's inverse penalty control for logistic regression and SVM.
C.effect: Larger C weakens regularization; small C can underfit. Scaling changes the trade-off.

l1_ratio.label: L1 fraction
l1_ratio.definition: Mixes sparse absolute-value and squared-weight penalties in elastic net.
l1_ratio.effect: Near one behaves more like lasso; near zero more like ridge.

neighbors.label: Number of neighbours k
neighbors.definition: The closest training examples voting on a new example.
neighbors.effect: Small k is flexible and noise-sensitive; larger k smooths boundaries.

neighbor_weights.label: Neighbour voting
neighbor_weights.definition: Equal votes or votes weighted by inverse distance.
neighbor_weights.effect: Distance weighting makes nearby examples more influential; duplicate points can dominate.

kernel.label: SVM kernel
kernel.definition: Linear uses a flat separator; RBF permits local curved boundaries.
kernel.effect: RBF flexibility depends jointly on C, feature scaling and gamma.

gamma.label: RBF gamma
gamma.definition: How quickly RBF similarity decays with squared distance.
gamma.effect: Larger gamma makes more local decisions and can overfit.

epsilon.label: Regression error tube ε
epsilon.definition: SVR ignores prediction errors inside an epsilon-wide tube in target units.
epsilon.effect: Larger epsilon permits more small errors; it changes the fitting objective, not the reported MAE.

smoothing.label: Variance smoothing
smoothing.definition: A stabilizing addition to Gaussian Naive Bayes feature variances.
smoothing.effect: Too little can be numerically fragile; too much can blur discrimination.

depth.label: Maximum tree depth
depth.definition: The longest allowed sequence of tree decisions. None allows growth until other rules stop it.
depth.effect: Deeper trees fit finer patterns but can memorize small training sets.

leaf.label: Minimum rows per leaf
leaf.definition: The minimum number of training rows in a final tree region.
leaf.effect: Larger leaves smooth predictions and reduce variance.

trees.label: Number of trees
trees.definition: Independent bootstrapped trees whose predictions are combined.
trees.effect: More trees reduce sampling noise but increase memory and fitting time.

rounds.label: Boosting rounds
rounds.definition: Sequential fitted trees correcting the current model's objective.
rounds.effect: More rounds increase capacity. This implementation disables internal early stopping for a transparent fixed budget.

boost_rate.label: Boosting learning rate
boost_rate.definition: Scales each newly added tree's contribution.
boost_rate.effect: Smaller values generally need more rounds; do not compare learning rate without its round budget.

clusters.label: Number of clusters
clusters.definition: The requested number of K-means groups or Gaussian mixture components.
clusters.effect: A requested group count is an assumption, not a discovered truth.

radius.label: DBSCAN neighbourhood radius
radius.definition: Maximum distance for neighbours after the selected scaling.
radius.effect: Small radius labels more points as noise; large radius can merge distinct groups.

min_samples.label: DBSCAN minimum neighbours
min_samples.definition: The local density requirement for a core point, including the point itself.
min_samples.effect: Larger requirements reject sparse regions. This lab reports DBSCAN fitting-set diagnostics only.

components.label: PCA components
components.definition: The number of orthogonal directions retained from training-set variance.
components.effect: More components reduce reconstruction error but compress less. High variance is not necessarily predictive signal.

contamination.label: Expected outlier fraction
contamination.effect: The chosen fraction sets a cutoff, not an independently estimated real-world prevalence.

epochs.label: Epochs
epochs.definition: One epoch visits every selected training row once.
epochs.effect: More epochs can improve fitting or overfit. The best development checkpoint is restored before the final test.

batch_size.label: Batch size
batch_size.definition: Examples contributing to one backward calculation and weight update.
batch_size.effect: Larger batches use more activation memory and yield fewer updates per epoch.

learning_rate.label: Learning rate
learning_rate.definition: The scale used by SGD or AdamW to change weights.
learning_rate.effect: Too large can destabilize learning; too small may appear not to learn. Compare with batch size and schedule.

optimizer.label: Optimizer
optimizer.definition: AdamW adapts per-parameter updates; SGD here uses momentum 0.9.
optimizer.effect: The same numerical learning rate is not equally suitable for both methods.

width.label: Hidden width / CNN channels
width.definition: MLP hidden units, or the channel count in the first convolution block.
width.effect: Wider layers increase capacity, parameter count and computation. CNN block two has twice this width.

layers.label: Hidden layers
layers.definition: The number of nonlinear hidden layers in an MLP.
layers.effect: Depth increases repeated transformations and may make optimization harder.

activation.label: Activation
activation.definition: The nonlinear transformation between learned linear layers.
activation.effect: Without nonlinearity stacked linear layers collapse into one linear map.

dropout.label: Dropout fraction
dropout.definition: Randomly zeros this fraction of hidden activations during training only.
dropout.effect: Can reduce co-adaptation; excessive dropout can prevent fitting. Evaluation disables it.

weight_decay.label: Weight decay
weight_decay.effect: AdamW uses decoupled decay; SGD implements L2-style decay. They are not numerically identical objectives.

normalization.label: Hidden normalization
normalization.definition: Layer uses LayerNorm in an MLP and one-group GroupNorm over channel/spatial values in a CNN (with channel-wise affine weights). Batch uses BatchNorm and running evaluation statistics.
normalization.effect: Normalization can stabilize optimization. Very small batches make batch norm noisy; the layer and spatial group variants are not identical parameterizations.

clip.label: Maximum gradient norm
clip.definition: Rescales a gradient if its total norm exceeds this value. Zero disables clipping.
clip.effect: Clipping limits large updates; it does not repair a wrong loss or leaked data.

schedule.label: Learning-rate schedule
schedule.definition: Keep the rate fixed or reduce it by a cosine across epochs.
schedule.effect: A falling rate can refine fitting; a short schedule may reduce it too early.

patience.label: Early-stopping patience
patience.definition: Stop after this many epochs without better development loss. Zero runs the full budget.
patience.effect: Uses development data only. The final model is the best development checkpoint even when early stopping is disabled.

device.label: Local processor
device.definition: Auto checks NVIDIA CUDA, Apple Metal, then CPU using installed PyTorch. Classical ML always uses CPU.
device.effect: Small workloads may be slower on a GPU. Detection is not a guarantee that your batch fits in memory. This lab never starts a cloud job.

def load(name, train_limit=5000, root=DATA, controls=None):
    if name not in CATALOG or type(train_limit) is not int or train_limit not in {500, 1500, 5000, 15000, 60000}:
        raise ValueError("Unknown dataset or training-row limit.")
    info = dict(CATALOG[name]); shape = None; groups = None; official = False
    if not ready(name, root):
        raise ValueError("Prepare this public dataset before training.")
    if name in {"sms_spam", "uci_har", "bike_sharing"}:
        from .sequence_data import load as load_sequence
        return load_sequence(name, train_limit, root, controls or {})
    if name in {"fashion_mnist", "mnist", "cifar10", "wine_red", "wine_white"}:
        folder = Path(root) / ("wine_quality" if name.startswith("wine_") else name)
        receipt = read_json(folder / "receipt.json")
        for filename, expected in receipt["files"].items():
            file = folder / filename
            if Path(filename).name != filename or file.is_symlink() or sha256(file) != expected:
                raise ValueError("Prepared dataset integrity check failed.")
        info["receipt"] = receipt
    if name in {"iris", "wine", "digits", "breast_cancer"}:
        item = getattr(datasets, "load_" + name)()
        x, y = item.data.astype(np.float32), item.target.astype(np.int64)
        info.update(feature_names=list(item.feature_names), class_names=[str(t) for t in item.target_names])
        if name == "digits":
            x = x / 16; shape = [1, 8, 8]
    elif name == "diabetes":
        item = datasets.load_diabetes(scaled=False)
        x, y = item.data.astype(np.float32), item.target.astype(np.float32)
        info["feature_names"] = list(item.feature_names)
    elif name.startswith("wine_"):
        with zipfile.ZipFile(folder / "wine_quality.zip") as archive:
            raw = archive.read("winequality-" + name.removeprefix("wine_") + ".csv")
        values = np.loadtxt(io.BytesIO(raw), delimiter=";", skiprows=1).astype(np.float32)
        x, y = values[:, :-1], values[:, -1]
        _, groups = np.unique(x, axis=0, return_inverse=True)
        info["feature_names"] = raw.decode().splitlines()[0].replace('"', '').split(";")[:-1]
    elif name in {"fashion_mnist", "mnist"}:
        x = np.concatenate([_idx(folder / "train-images-idx3-ubyte.gz", True), _idx(folder / "t10k-images-idx3-ubyte.gz", True)])
        y = np.concatenate([_idx(folder / "train-labels-idx1-ubyte.gz", False), _idx(folder / "t10k-labels-idx1-ubyte.gz", False)])
        shape = [1, 28, 28]; official = True
        info["class_names"] = ["T-shirt/top", "Trouser", "Pullover", "Dress", "Coat", "Sandal", "Shirt", "Sneaker", "Bag", "Ankle boot"] if name == "fashion_mnist" else [str(i) for i in range(10)]
    elif name == "cifar10":
        with tarfile.open(folder / "cifar-10-binary.tar.gz", "r:gz") as archive:
            batches = [_cifar_batch(archive, f"data_batch_{i}.bin") for i in range(1, 6)] + [_cifar_batch(archive, "test_batch.bin")]
        x = np.concatenate([b[0] for b in batches]).astype(np.float32) / 255
        y = np.concatenate([b[1] for b in batches]); shape = [3, 32, 32]; official = True
        info["class_names"] = ["airplane", "automobile", "bird", "cat", "deer", "dog", "frog", "horse", "ship", "truck"]
    else:
        rng = np.random.default_rng(SPLIT_SEED)
        if name == "curve":
            x = rng.uniform(-3, 3, (2400, 6)).astype(np.float32)
            y = (2 * np.sin(x[:, 0]) + .4 * x[:, 1]**2 - x[:, 2] + rng.normal(0, .4, 2400)).astype(np.float32)
        else:
            centers = np.array([[-2, -1], [2, 1], [0, 3]])
            y = np.concatenate([np.repeat(np.arange(3), [400, 350, 330]), np.repeat(-1, 120)])
            x = np.concatenate([rng.normal(centers[k], [.5, .65, .4][k], (n, 2)) for k, n in enumerate([400, 350, 330])] + [rng.uniform(-5, 5, (120, 2))]).astype(np.float32)
        info["feature_names"] = ["x" + str(i) for i in range(x.shape[1])]
    indices = np.arange(len(x))
    if official:
        original_train = 50000 if name == "cifar10" else 60000
        train, dev = train_test_split(indices[:original_train], test_size=10000, random_state=SPLIT_SEED, stratify=y[:original_train])
        test = indices[original_train:]
        policy = f"{original_train-10000:,} fitting / 10,000 development from original train; 10,000 original test untouched by fitting."
    elif groups is not None:
        train_dev, test = next(GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=.2, random_state=SPLIT_SEED).split(x, y, groups))
        a, b = next(GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=.25, random_state=SPLIT_SEED).split(x[train_dev], y[train_dev], groups[train_dev]))
        train, dev = train_dev[a], train_dev[b]
        policy = "Approximately 60/20/20; exact identical feature rows grouped, including differing ratings."
    else:
        stratify = y if info["task"] == "classification" else None
        train_dev, test = train_test_split(indices, test_size=.2, random_state=SPLIT_SEED, stratify=stratify)
        train, dev = train_test_split(train_dev, test_size=.25, random_state=SPLIT_SEED, stratify=y[train_dev] if stratify is not None else None)
        policy = "Fixed 60/20/20 split; stratified only for labelled classification."
    full_train = len(train)
    if full_train > train_limit:
        train, _ = train_test_split(train, train_size=train_limit, random_state=SPLIT_SEED + 1,
                                    stratify=y[train] if info["task"] == "classification" else None)
    split_ids = {"train": train.tolist(), "dev": dev.tolist(), "test": test.tolist()}
    fingerprint = hashlib.sha256(x.tobytes() + y.tobytes()).hexdigest()
    import json
    split_hash = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(split_ids, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
    info.update(id=name, rows=len(x), features=x.shape[1], image_shape=shape, fingerprint=fingerprint,
                split_fingerprint=split_hash, split_seed=SPLIT_SEED, split_policy=policy,
                counts={k: len(v) for k, v in split_ids.items()}, available_train=full_train,
                warning="Repeatedly viewing test scores makes this an exploratory lab, not a fresh confirmatory benchmark.")
    return {"x": x, "y": y, "groups":groups, "indices": {"train": train, "dev": dev, "test": test}, "info": info, "split_ids": split_ids}

def load(name, train_limit, root, controls):
    from .model_data import CATALOG, SPLIT_SEED
    folder = Path(root) / name
    if folder.is_symlink(): raise ValueError("Dataset symlink is not allowed.")
    receipt = read_json(folder / "receipt.json"); file = folder / "source.zip"
    if file.is_symlink() or set(receipt["files"]) != {"source.zip"} or sha256(file) != receipt["files"]["source.zip"]:
        raise ValueError("Prepared sequence dataset integrity check failed.")
    info = dict(CATALOG[name]); extras = {}; groups = None
    with zipfile.ZipFile(file) as archive:
        if name == "sms_spam":
            texts, y = sms_rows(archive); indices = np.arange(len(y))
            train_dev, test = train_test_split(indices, test_size=.2, stratify=y, random_state=SPLIT_SEED)
            train, dev = train_test_split(train_dev, test_size=.25, stratify=y[train_dev], random_state=SPLIT_SEED)
            policy = "Identical normalized messages deduplicated before a fixed stratified 60/20/20 split. Vocabulary fitted on selected training texts only."
            info.update(class_names=["ham", "spam"])
            extras["texts"] = texts
        elif name == "uci_har":
            windows, y, groups, original, channels = har_rows(archive)
            available = np.flatnonzero(original == "train"); test = np.flatnonzero(original == "test")
            a, b = next(GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=.25, random_state=SPLIT_SEED).split(available, y[available], groups[available]))
            train, dev = available[a], available[b]
            x = windows.reshape(len(y), -1)
            info.update(sequence_shape=[128, 9], class_names=["walking", "walking upstairs", "walking downstairs", "sitting", "standing", "laying"], channel_names=channels)
            policy = "Original subject-disjoint test retained; development uses separate participants from original training. Overlapping windows from one person never cross splits."
            extras["subjects"] = groups
        else:
            histories, y, times = bike_rows(archive); n = len(y)
            a, b = int(n * .6), int(n * .8)
            train, dev, test = np.arange(a), np.arange(a, b), np.arange(b, n)
            lookback = controls.get("lookback", 24)
            x = histories[:, -lookback:].copy()
            info.update(sequence_shape=[lookback, 1], target_units="rentals in the next hour", target_times=times,
                        feature_names=[f"count {i} hours before target" for i in range(lookback, 0, -1)])
            extras.update(persistence=histories[:, -1].copy(), target_times=times)
            policy = "Chronological 60/20/20 target hours. Every target has 96 complete preceding hours; selected lookback uses only those observed past counts. Rolling one-hour forecasts, not recursive multi-step forecasts. Training cap retains the most recent fitting hours."
    full_train = len(train)
    if full_train > train_limit:
        if name == "bike_sharing": train = train[-train_limit:]
        else:
            train, _ = train_test_split(train, train_size=train_limit, stratify=y[train], random_state=SPLIT_SEED + 1)
    input_spec = {"kind": info["kind"]}
    if name == "sms_spam":
        x, vocabulary = encode_text(extras["texts"], train, controls.get("max_tokens", 128), controls.get("vocab_size", 5000))
        info["sequence_shape"] = [x.shape[1], 1]
        input_spec.update(vocabulary_size=len(vocabulary) + 2)
        extras["vocabulary"] = vocabulary
    input_spec.update(sequence_shape=info["sequence_shape"], forecast=name == "bike_sharing")
    split_ids = {"train": train.tolist(), "dev": dev.tolist(), "test": test.tolist()}
    # Identity is the raw source/cohort, not a tokenizer or lookback representation.
    fingerprint = hashlib.sha256((name + receipt["files"]["source.zip"]).encode()).hexdigest()
    info.update(id=name, rows=len(y), features=x.shape[1], image_shape=None, input_kind=info["kind"], input_spec=input_spec,
                fingerprint=fingerprint, split_fingerprint=hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(split_ids, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest(),
                split_seed=SPLIT_SEED, split_policy=policy, counts={k: len(v) for k, v in split_ids.items()}, available_train=full_train,
                receipt=receipt, warning="Test viewing is exploratory. Subject dependence and temporal dependence require appropriate uncertainty estimates, not independent-row intervals.")
    return {"x": x, "y": y, "groups": groups, "indices": {"train": train, "dev": dev, "test": test},
            "split_ids": split_ids, "info": info, **extras}

class EncoderBlock(nn.Module):
    """Pre-norm bidirectional self-attention, then a position-wise MLP.

    Mask keys before softmax and clear padded queries after the residual path.
    Explicit operations keep the teaching code and CPU/MPS execution aligned.
    """
    def __init__(self, width, heads, dropout):
        super().__init__()
        self.heads = heads
        self.norm1, self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(width), nn.LayerNorm(width)
        self.qkv, self.projection = nn.Linear(width, 3 * width), nn.Linear(width, width)
        self.drop = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        self.ff = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(width, 4 * width), nn.GELU(), nn.Dropout(dropout), nn.Linear(4 * width, width))

    def forward(self, x, valid):
        batch, length, width = x.shape
        q, k, v = self.qkv(self.norm1(x)).reshape(batch, length, 3, self.heads, width // self.heads).permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4).unbind(0)
        scores = (q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) / (width // self.heads) ** .5
        weights = scores.masked_fill(~valid[:, None, None, :], float("-inf")).softmax(-1)
        attended = (self.drop(weights) @ v).transpose(1, 2).reshape(batch, length, width)
        x = x + self.drop(self.projection(attended))
        return (x + self.drop(self.ff(self.norm2(x)))) * valid.unsqueeze(-1)

def _neural(settings, data, directory, update):
    import torch
    from torch import nn
    from torch.utils.tensorboard import SummaryWriter
    p = settings["controls"]; task = settings["task"]; ids = data["indices"]
    torch.set_num_threads(2); torch.manual_seed(p["seed"])
    np.random.seed(p["seed"])
    device = choose_device(p["device"])
    from .sequence_data import neural_inputs
    x, preprocess, input_spec = neural_inputs(data)
    y = data["y"].copy(); shape = data["info"]["image_shape"]
    target_mean, target_scale = 0.0, 1.0
    if task == "regression":
        target_mean, target_scale = float(y[ids["train"]].mean()), max(float(y[ids["train"]].std()), 1e-6)
        y_train = ((y - target_mean) / target_scale).astype(np.float32)
    else: y_train = y
    labels = np.unique(y) if task == "classification" else None
    n_outputs = len(labels) if labels is not None else 1
    model = network(settings["model"], p, x.shape[1], n_outputs, shape, input_spec).to(device)
    count = sum(t.numel() for t in model.parameters())
    if count > 3_000_000: raise ValueError("This local configuration exceeds three million parameters.")
    x_tensor = torch.from_numpy(x)
    device_note = "Requested processor supports this configuration."
    if device != "cpu" and settings["model"] in {*SEQUENCE_NAMES, "cnn1d", "tcn", "embedding_mean", "transformer_encoder", "vit"}:
        # Probe actual model operations, not just a generic matrix multiplication.
        from .sequence_models import probe_training_device
        try:
            probe_training_device(model, x_tensor[ids["train"][:2]], device)
        except (RuntimeError, NotImplementedError) as exc:
            if p["device"] != "auto": raise ValueError("This model is unsupported on the requested processor; select CPU. " + str(exc)[:180]) from exc
            device_note = "Auto fell back to CPU after this model's processor check: " + str(exc)[:180]
            device = "cpu"; model.to(device); model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
    y_tensor = torch.from_numpy(y_train.astype(np.int64 if task == "classification" else np.float32))
    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss() if task == "classification" else nn.MSELoss()
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=p["learning_rate"], weight_decay=p["weight_decay"]) if p["optimizer"] == "adamw" else torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=p["learning_rate"], momentum=.9, weight_decay=p["weight_decay"])
    history = []; best = math.inf; best_state = None; best_epoch = 0; stale = 0; updates = 0
    writer = SummaryWriter(str(directory / "tensorboard"))
    def evaluate(split):
        model.eval(); predictions = []; total = 0.; seen = 0
        evaluation_batch = min(256, p["batch_size"])
        with torch.no_grad():
            for start in range(0, len(ids[split]), evaluation_batch):
                rows = ids[split][start:start+evaluation_batch]; bx = x_tensor[rows].to(device)
                target = bx if task == "representation" else y_tensor[rows].to(device)
                output = model(bx)
                if task == "regression": output = output.squeeze(-1)
                loss = criterion(output, target)

                if batch_no % 10 == 0:

            if improved:

            else: stale += 1

            history.append(row); write_json(directory / "history.json", history)
            for key in ["train_loss", "dev_loss", "learning_rate", "mean_gradient_norm_before_clipping"]: writer.add_scalar(key, row[key], epoch)
            writer.flush()
            update(phase=f"Completed epoch {epoch}", completed_epochs=epoch, epoch_fraction=epoch, best_epoch=best_epoch, elapsed_seconds=row["elapsed_seconds"], updates=updates)

        torch.save({"state_dict": best_state, "settings": settings, "features": x.shape[1], "outputs": n_outputs, "image_shape": shape,
                    "input_spec":input_spec, "preprocessing": preprocess, "target_transform": {"mean": target_mean, "scale": target_scale}}, directory / "weights.pt")

        result = {"history": history, "best_epoch": best_epoch, "parameters": count, "device": device,

        if task in {"classification", "regression"}:

                    shifted = raw - raw.max(axis=1, keepdims=True); prob = np.exp(shifted); prob /= prob.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)

            result["predictions"] = _prediction_artifact(data, outputs, task)
        else:

def neural_inputs(data):
    """Training-only per-channel scaling; never standardize integer token IDs."""
    from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
    x = data["x"].copy(); info = data["info"]; train = data["indices"]["train"]
    spec = info.get("input_spec", {"kind": "image" if info["image_shape"] else "table"})
    if spec["kind"] == "text":
        return x, {"kind": "train-only vocabulary; PAD=0, UNK=1; right padding masked", "vocabulary": data["vocabulary"]}, spec
    if spec["kind"] == "sequence":
        shaped = x.reshape(-1, *spec["sequence_shape"])
        values = shaped[train].reshape(-1, shaped.shape[-1])
        mean, scale = values.mean(0), np.maximum(values.std(0), 1e-6)
        x = ((shaped - mean) / scale).reshape(len(x), -1).astype(np.float32)
        return x, {"kind": "training-only per-channel standardization", "mean": mean.tolist(), "scale": scale.tolist()}, spec
    if info["image_shape"]:
        c, h, w = info["image_shape"]
        return x, {"kind": "fixed image range 0–1"}, {"kind": "image", "sequence_shape": [h, c*w]}
    scaler = StandardScaler().fit(x[train])
    return scaler.transform(x).astype(np.float32), {"kind": "training-only standardization", "mean": scaler.mean_.tolist(), "scale": scaler.scale_.tolist()}, spec

def conversations():
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq
    rows=[];seen=set()
    for file,expected in DATA_FILES.items():
        path=DATA_DIR/"data"/file
        if sha256(path)!=expected:raise ValueError("Prepared conversation data changed; prepare it again.")
        for record in pq.read_table(path).to_pylist():
            messages=record["messages"]
            canonical="\n".join(m["content"].strip() for m in messages)
            group=hashlib.sha256(canonical.casefold().encode()).hexdigest()
            if group in seen:continue
            seen.add(group)
            split="test" if file.startswith("test") else "dev" if int(group[:8],16)%10==0 else "train"
            # Group by full conversation; all turns from one conversation stay in one split.
            for i,m in enumerate(messages):
                if m["role"]!="assistant" or i<3:continue # skip the generic greeting exchange
                if messages[i-1]["role"]!="user":continue
                rows.append({"id":group[:16]+"-"+str(i),"group":group,"split":split,
                    "messages":messages[:i+1],"text":messages[i-1]["content"]+"\n"+m["content"],
                    "prompt":messages[i-1]["content"],"answer":m["content"]})
    return rows

def encode_example(row,tokenizer,maximum):
    # Preserve the supplied chat template; mask prompt positions, not EOS token IDs.
    # The immediate exchange is a self-contained bounded task; earlier turns are omitted.
    messages=[{"role":"user","content":row["prompt"]},{"role":"assistant","content":row["answer"]}]
    prompt=tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages[:1],tokenize=True,add_generation_prompt=True)
    full=tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages,tokenize=True,add_generation_prompt=False)
    if full[:len(prompt)]!=prompt:raise ValueError("Chat template prefix is not stable; cannot mask safely.")
    if len(prompt)>=maximum-8:return None
    full=full[:maximum]
    labels=[-100]*len(prompt)+full[len(prompt):]
    if sum(x!=-100 for x in labels)<4:return None
    return {"ids":full,"labels":labels,"id":row["id"],"group":row["group"]}

def prepared_data(tokenizer,settings):
    rows=conversations();encoded={s:[] for s in ["train","dev","test"]};docs=[]
    seen=set()
    # Stable text-level duplicate filtering across all retained examples as well as group separation.
    for row in sorted(rows,key=lambda r:(r["split"]!="test",r["split"]!="dev",r["id"])):
        key=hashlib.sha256(" ".join(row["text"].casefold().split()).encode()).hexdigest()
        if key in seen:continue
        item=encode_example(row,tokenizer,settings["block_size"])
        limit=settings["examples"] if row["split"]=="train" else 16
        if item is None or len(encoded[row["split"]])>=limit:continue
        seen.add(key);encoded[row["split"]].append(item)
        docs.append({k:row[k] for k in ["id","group","split","text","prompt","answer"]})
    if min(map(len,encoded.values()))<4:raise ValueError("Too few valid train/dev/test examples after masking.")
    return encoded,docs

def load_base(device):
    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM,AutoTokenizer
    if not status()["ready"]:raise ValueError("Local language model/data are not prepared. Run: python lab.py prepare --model")
    tokenizer=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_DIR,local_files_only=True,trust_remote_code=False)
    if tokenizer.pad_token_id is None:tokenizer.pad_token=tokenizer.eos_token
    model=AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MODEL_DIR,local_files_only=True,trust_remote_code=False,
        use_safetensors=True,dtype=torch.float32,attn_implementation="eager").to(device)
    return model,tokenizer

def train(name,settings=None,runs_root=RUNS):
    from peft import LoraConfig,get_peft_model
    settings=validate(settings);device=choose_device(settings["device"])
    torch.set_num_threads(4);torch.manual_seed(settings["seed"]);random.seed(settings["seed"])
    directory=run_path(name,runs_root);directory.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=False)
    started=time.perf_counter();metrics=[];writer=None
    manifest={"schema_version":3,"id":name,"engine":"lora","status":"RUNNING","phase":"Loading the pretrained model",
        "purpose":"local_instruction_adaptation","started_at":datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),"completed_steps":0,
        "requested_steps":settings["steps"],"settings":settings,"source_hashes":source_hashes(),
        "model":{"parameters":361821120,"name":MODEL_ID},"hardware":{"device":device,"torch":str(torch.__version__),"machine":platform.machine()},
        "evaluation_protocol":"assistant_only_conversation_v1","config":{"tokenizer":{"repo":MODEL_ID,"revision":MODEL_REVISION},"model":{"name":MODEL_ID}},
        "limits":["Language competence comes from the pretrained model, not this short local adaptation.",
                  "Conversation data is synthetic and may have been seen during original SmolLM training.",
                  "Only assistant response tokens contribute to loss; reported loss is not directly comparable to scratch runs.",
                  "Adapters may improve or hurt behaviour. Short runs do not establish general quality."]}
    write_json(directory/"manifest.json",manifest);write_json(directory/"metrics.json",metrics)
    def progress(phase,**values):
        elapsed=time.perf_counter()-started
        manifest.update(phase=phase,elapsed_seconds=elapsed,updated_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),**values)
        write_json(directory/"manifest.json",manifest)
    try:
        model,tokenizer=load_base(device);items,docs=prepared_data(tokenizer,settings)
        write_json(directory/"data.json",{"license":"Apache-2.0","repo":DATA_ID,"revision":DATA_REVISION,"synthetic":True,
            "documents":docs,"counts":dict(Counter(d["split"] for d in docs)),"masking":"Immediate user/assistant exchange; prompt labels -100; real EOS retained; padding never targets.",
            "overlap_warning":"Held out only from local adaptation, not proven absent from original pretraining/SFT."})
        write_json(directory/"tokenizer.json",{"engine":"huggingface","repo":MODEL_ID,"revision":MODEL_REVISION})
        progress("Measuring the original model")
        baseline={s:evaluate(model,items[s],device) for s in ["dev","test"]}
        baseline_samples=[{"prompt":p,"completion":sample(model,tokenizer,p,device,seed=settings["seed"]),"stage":"Before adaptation"} for p in PROMPTS]
        write_json(directory/"baseline.json",{"evaluation":baseline,"samples":baseline_samples})
        model=get_peft_model(model,LoraConfig(r=settings["rank"],lora_alpha=2*settings["rank"],lora_dropout=0.05,
            target_modules=["q_proj","v_proj"],bias="none",task_type="CAUSAL_LM"))
        trainable=sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
        manifest["model"].update(trainable_parameters=trainable,rank=settings["rank"])
        optimizer=torch.optim.AdamW([p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad],lr=settings["learning_rate"])
        writer=Telemetry(directory);sampler=random.Random(settings["seed"]);best=baseline["dev"]["nll"]
        # Save the zero-update adapter too: adaptation cannot silently replace a better baseline.
        model.save_pretrained(directory/"adapter",safe_serialization=True)
        best_step=0;exposures=0;train_started=time.perf_counter()
        metrics.append({"step":0,"dev_nll":baseline["dev"]["nll"],"tokens_processed":0,"elapsed_seconds":time.perf_counter()-started})
        for step in range(1,settings["steps"]+1):
            progress("Training the adapters",completed_steps=step-1)
            model.train();optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            chosen=[sampler.choice(items["train"]) for _ in range(settings["accumulation"])]
            valid_total=sum(sum(v!=-100 for v in item["labels"][1:]) for item in chosen)
            total=0.
            for item in chosen:
                x,y=tensors(item,device);valid=int((y[:,1:]!=-100).sum())
                loss=model(input_ids=x,labels=y,use_cache=False).loss
                if not torch.isfinite(loss):raise ValueError("Non-finite loss; training stopped.")
                (loss*valid/valid_total).backward();total+=float(loss.detach())*valid
            norm=float(torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_([p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad],1.))
            if not math.isfinite(norm):raise ValueError("Non-finite gradient; training stopped.")
            optimizer.step();exposures+=valid_total;synchronize(device)
            elapsed=time.perf_counter()-train_started
            row={"step":step,"sampled_train_nll":total/valid_total,"learning_rate":settings["learning_rate"],
                 "gradient_norm_pre_clip":norm,"tokens_processed":exposures,"tokens_per_second":exposures/max(elapsed,1e-6),
                 "elapsed_seconds":time.perf_counter()-started}
            if step==1 or step%10==0 or step==settings["steps"]:
                progress("Checking held-out responses",completed_steps=step)
                dev=evaluate(model,items["dev"],device);row["dev_nll"]=dev["nll"]
                if dev["nll"]<best:
                    best=dev["nll"];best_step=step;model.save_pretrained(directory/"adapter",safe_serialization=True)
            metrics.append(row);writer.log(row);write_json(directory/"metrics.json",metrics)
            progress("Training the adapters",completed_steps=step,tokens_processed=exposures,
                     tokens_per_second=row["tokens_per_second"],eta_seconds=elapsed/step*(settings["steps"]-step))
        model.save_pretrained(directory/"adapter-last",safe_serialization=True)
        from peft import set_peft_model_state_dict
        from safetensors.torch import load_file
        set_peft_model_state_dict(model,load_file(str(directory/"adapter"/"adapter_model.safetensors")))
        progress("Evaluating the selected checkpoint",completed_steps=settings["steps"])
        final={s:evaluate(model,items[s],device) for s in ["dev","test"]}
        write_json(directory/"evaluation.json",{"checkpoint_step":best_step,"transformer":final,"pretrained":baseline,
            "selection":"Lowest local development loss, including the zero-update pretrained baseline.","units":"nats per assistant response token"})
        after=[{"prompt":p,"completion":sample(model,tokenizer,p,device,seed=settings["seed"]),"stage":"Selected adapter"} for p in PROMPTS]
        write_json(directory/"samples.json",baseline_samples+after)
        # Seal adapter contents through a top-level digest file as well as the common manifest.
        write_json(directory/"adapter_files.json",{str(p.relative_to(directory)):sha256(p) for p in directory.glob("adapter*/*") if p.is_file()})
        progress("Complete",status="MEASURED",best_checkpoint_step=best_step,training_seconds=time.perf_counter()-started,eta_seconds=0)
    except BaseException as exc:
        progress("Stopped" if isinstance(exc,KeyboardInterrupt) else "Failed",status="CANCELLED" if isinstance(exc,KeyboardInterrupt) else "FAILED",error=str(exc))
        raise
    finally:
        if writer:writer.close()
        seal(directory)
    return manifest
